5b58a02d.text: Shapes must fit like pipes: what comes out of one layer must go into the next.

75b6ef59.text: Splendid! Every filter hunts for its own pattern, so try the next job.

b8e4fc27.text: Fixed-wing: wings make lift, so it flies far and fast! But it can never hover.

dc3752a2.text: A quadcopter: four rotors, great at hovering! ReSeed's prototype is an X500-class quad.

fb1b2385.text: Octocopter: eight rotors share the heavy load! Many can still land if one motor fails, but not all.

53f39852.text: VTOL hybrid: it takes off straight up, then uses its wings to cruise far like a plane!

497ea179.text: 💡 Sort the five numbers in your head: two come before the middle one and two come after it. The middle is the 3rd.

92574112.text: Single-rotor helicopter! One big rotor is very efficient for long, heavy work.

2abe2b7e.text: Hexacopter: six rotors share the load! Many can land on the other five, if they are set up for it.

942288e8.text: All parts in, now the propellers! If all four spin the same way, the whole drone twists around.

0ba9439c.text: RTL: fly home now, while there's still enough battery! ReSeed's battery plans keep a 25 % reserve for this.

af694244.text: LAND: RTL and HOLD need GPS to know where the drone is! Come down gently, right now.

f89f66d7.text: RTL: if the failsafe is set up, the drone uses GPS to fly home when the radio is lost! It needs a good GPS fix and a saved home point.

f46f1a76.text: HOLD: stop and hover in place until they have walked past! Never fly over people.

023170ec.text: RTL! Plenty of battery and good GPS: head home before the storm arrives.

67928859.text: Props across from each other spin the same way. Props side by side spin opposite ways.

71cbb5ef.text: LAND: it's too far to make it home on 8 %! Land now in a clear spot, and an adult can fetch it.

eefde7a7.text: For each alarm, pick a flight mode: RTL flies home, LAND comes down, HOLD hovers.

5c98273a.text: Final challenge: turn our detective rule into an if / elif chain, like in Python.

c8b90d65.text: RESEED needs a drop of 0.20 or more (or 25 %) in two recent seasons. Inspect the clues, then stamp!

cb325ad7.text: But forests can heal by themselves. A big dip that is back to green means RECOVERING: don't seed!

0819bd1f.text: Fires and saws leave a clue in short-wave infrared light. A drop of 0.10 in NBR hints at burning or clearing.

25a06d41.text: Drag each question into a slot and give it a verdict stamp. Then run it on all thirteen cases!

937daf67.text: Yes, it's just winter! The oaks drop their leaves, and every summer they come back.

b7093606.text: Correct! Shrubs grew back after the fire, but big patches of conifers are still gone.

4f838a2d.text: Wow, you spotted it! The fire was huge, but the eucalypts sprouted again and the forest seems to be healing by itself.

b72b09df.text: Look closely: small patches, about 10 hectares in total, dropped in both recent seasons.

05d2ddf2.text: AI language models don't read letters. They read tokens: little chunks of text.

63dde563.text: Short, common words stay whole, and long or made-up words get chopped. You run the chopper!

71e34a0b.text: In this game, a model's weights must fit in GPU memory: billions of settings × bytes each. 16 bits are 2 bytes, and 4 bits are half a byte.

c062adec.text: Two ways to serve an AI model. vLLM is a big kitchen that cooks for many users at once on server GPUs.

6d4c9abc.text: llama.cpp is a food truck: it runs a GGUF model that fits on your laptop. Send each customer to the right one!

f1524d54.text: How many tokens did this sentence make? Count the blocks!

9657cd05.text: Last job: a long chat! Watch the KV cache grow as the chat gets longer.

e51252de.text: Open the big kitchen on the server GPUs! Which command starts it?

da6e1a92.text: Rush hour: twelve hungry customers wait at each place! Who serves all twelve first?

565fb158.text: Crash! CUDA out of memory means it didn't fit, so read the gauge and pick a fix.

93a04d89.text: 💡 Short words we use every day stay whole. Names and made-up words get chopped!

9478e1ff.text: Welcome to Score island! I'm Professor Hoot, and I measure how healthy forests are.

4c129267.text: From space, a farm and a forest can both look green. We need a cleverer way to see!

2da138ee.text: You can read the invisible glow of leaves now. That number is NDVI!

45094047.text: Put on the near-infrared goggles! They show a light our eyes cannot see.

bb6cb695.text: Slide them over the forest, lawn, road, lake, snow and roof. Hold still to scan each one.

df66867e.text: Tap a bin or press keys 1 to 5. Start at the top of the ladder.

2837395a.text: ReSeed gives every NDVI number one of five health classes. The sorter only sees the number!

e2715cfd.text: I brought real pictures from the Sentinel-2 satellite! This is your site, seen from space.

5168c0ec.text: Slide the goggles over it to see the real NDVI map. Then read the colour under each pin.

cc2c1fb8.text: Leaves glow in near-infrared. What else glowed really bright?

60c6d6c8.text: Yes! Snow also bounces back lots of red light, so we compare NIR with red to find real leaves.

29b6ac07.text: Snow fooled us, so we use two numbers: NIR and Red. Leaves bounce NIR and soak up red.

dde8f066.text: The NDVI machine does (NIR − Red) ÷ (NIR + Red). You do the sums, it does the rest!

bc0c36a0.text: Look again: the snow glowed bright white! Snow bounces back red light too, so we must compare NIR with red.

c97a4e81.text: You can't push it past the ends: NDVI stays between −1 and +1. Only 0 and 0 gives no answer at all!

95dda381.text: Perfect: low NDVI is a clue, not a reason. The next island checks it isn't just winter!

dde58fba.text: That's the real NDVI map ReSeed made for your site! Now let's watch NDVI change over a year.

4351d84e.text: Here is your site's wave too. Every month had a clear picture this year!

1441dce0.text: 💡 Hold the goggles still over a thing until the yellow ring fills. Space hops to the next one.

d8aefb54.text: Here is your site's wave too. Gaps are months with no clear picture, often because of clouds, so ReSeed leaves a gap instead of guessing.

c9540d92.text: Permission denied! Changing the whole computer needs boss powers.

a7860819.text: Then we tell the computer to start from the stick. Careful which drive you pick!

db16d665.text: Then make a pretend user with a strong password. Never type a real password into a game!

a9f90ceb.text: Our mission computer is built, but its screen is empty. It has no brain yet!

11da7b97.text: Squawk, I'm Tuki! Satellite pictures often travel across the internet before they reach us.

8f0bdcb1.text: Big pictures get cut into small packets. Let's run the Packet Post and deliver them all!

eb8bc517.text: Handshakes, parcels, live video, phone books and doors. You run the internet's post office now!

b6c88a58.text: Hoo, your forest pictures reached my lab safely! Next stop: is it really a forest?

93981ab6.text: Before TCP sends a picture, two computers shake hands: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK.

fbaa7ee9.text: Your forest picture is too big for one trip. Cut it into numbered packets and send them through the routers!

bc7a623a.text: Send SYN, then press ACK right when the SYN-ACK reaches your ring. Keys 1, 2 and 3 work too!

197ae44c.text: Packets may arrive mixed up, or not at all. Check the numbers, ask for a resend, then rebuild the picture.

34216dc1.text: G'day, my drone streams live video with UDP! Each video picture, a frame, travels as 4 packets that can get lost or mixed up.

9ed21875.text: In this game, one missing piece means Conceal: patch it with the last frame's piece. Two or more missing means Skip that frame.

eb177d6e.text: DNS is the internet's phone book. Find each name, and remember: your laptop keeps a cache of answers.

08927b5e.text: One computer has thousands of numbered doors called ports. Each program listens at its own door.

9d589c3b.text: To send packets, computers need an IP address. Older IPv4 addresses are four numbers with dots; newer IPv6 ones are longer.

d5830b19.text: A packet of this frame got lost! Should the video app wait for it to be sent again?

00388397.text: Read the label and pick the door: 443 HTTPS, 80 HTTP, 22 SSH, 8000 for python -m reseed serve.

7a6b52e3.text: Hoo, a perfect picture! Now a bigger one: twelve packets, and two Glitch Bugs on the road!

0f7ce987.text: Right, there's no time to wait here! Patch the hole or skip the frame, and keep going.

bb98b015.text: So which brain should our ReSeed mission computer get?

5cade4a2.text: The video froze, and my drone already flew past! UDP never resends by itself, and live video rarely has time to wait.

1c31a90f.text: 💡 Find the smallest number in the tray first, then the next one up.

847a533f.text: 💡 Watch the shrinking ring. Press the glowing button when the ring hugs the envelope!

82f57100.text: 💡 Count along the tray: 1, 2, 3… The number you cannot find is the missing one.

4d05187e.text: 💡 One red hole means Conceal, two or more mean Skip. Decide before the ring runs out!

f7ea44e5.text: 💡 Read the name letter by letter. Open its first-letter tab, then find the exact same name.

07399126.text: 💡 A number after a colon, like :8000, names the door. With no number, https means 443, http means 80 and ssh means 22.

af33d919.text: ReSeed looks for a 0.20 greenness drop from an earlier peak, in two recent growing seasons. That's a clue to forest loss.

2ff421fc.text: It's called DECLINEABS in config.py. Want to see the real mask ReSeed painted?

f2bf5c12.text: Then the drones know exactly where to fly. Grab your paint bucket!

ad54460d.text: Beaut, now I know exactly where to fly! See you on Fly island.

a689f656.text: Each square is a pixel. Its number says how much greener it used to be.

543d8a49.text: Lit squares that touch make one patch. My paint bucket finds them with flood fill.

e1ae2e69.text: Slide the threshold: squares at or above it light up. Light up the lost forest, not the noise!

b23ccfce.text: Tap a lit square. The paint spreads up, down, left and right, like water!

b64a1041.text: One pixel is 10 m by 10 m. That's 0.01 hectares.

f4a75cff.text: Let's count a big square first. Tap it with the bucket!

f0f774f3.text: The drones need the biggest patches first. Let's sort them, largest first!

33c84950.text: These are the real patch sizes from your site. Compare two cards at a time.

4f1beb13.text: G'day! ReSeed plans at most 50 hectares per mission, so bigger patches need cutting.

07f35e0a.text: Map two: land burned by a fire. Its edges are trickier!

67d74462.text: Slide the threshold up a bit. Then fewer squares light up.

98029b64.text: First, pick the patch for our first mission. Then slice the giant into drone-sized squares!

7b2918b2.text: Some lost squares stayed dark. Slide the threshold down a bit.

fdd88bdb.text: 💡 Look at the bar chart. Put the red line in the gap between the two hills.

64172850.text: You predicted it! Blobs that only touch at a corner are separate patches.

e9004a64.text: Tricky, right? Blobs that only touch at a corner are separate patches.

54ee274a.text: Whoa, the paint stopped at a corner! Only up, down, left and right count as neighbours.

a8883861.text: 💡 Tap any cream square. The paint does the rest!

a6bc301d.text: 💡 On this game map, lost forest has big drops and healthy forest only wiggles. Find the gap!

89ca24bd.text: Not quite! Think of 100 pennies: how many dollars is that?

9bb0b9e9.text: Speckle swept! Only patches of half a hectare or more stay on ReSeed's map.

bef154e3.text: Yes! One hectare is 100 m by 100 m, a bit bigger than a soccer field.

2b88ffb5.text: 💡 50 pixels make 0.5 ha. Fewer than 50 pixels means sweep it!

be0028b8.text: Now sweep the speckle! ReSeed skips patches smaller than 0.5 ha, even though some may be real.

4829d562.text: 💡 Each pixel is 0.01 ha. So 50 pixels make 0.5 ha.

47b5b13e.text: Sorted, just like ReSeed's list: rank 1 is the biggest. Now race the computer!

d2129623.text: 💡 Only two cards at a time. Bigger one on the left!

4bdafbf8.text: Python's sort() is called Timsort. For short lists like ours, it uses insertion sort: tuck each card into its spot!

36077244.text: 💡 Read the numbers. The bigger number must sit on the left.

98afbf1e.text: 💡 Skip every card over 50 ha. The first one left is the winner!

f806993f.text: Your site has no giant patch. Let's help the team in Rondônia with theirs!

eeb10334.text: 💡 A 700 m square is 49 hectares. Try it!

dc71b29d.text: 100 pixels, and each one is 0.01 hectares. How many hectares is that?

0c367d4e.text: ReSeed does this in splitpatch: squares about 707 m wide. A 707 m square is about 50 hectares.

03fb6b64.text: A brand-new cauldron! But look at the prompt: it still says (base).

ba0f1280.text: Next stop: my workshop. Every cauldron needs a computer to sit on!

95d6c0e2.text: Typing every potion by hand is slow. ReSeed keeps a recipe file called environment.yml.

3d557610.text: We're in the ndvi-app folder. Make the cauldron, step in, then pour in rasterio!

81d9dc94.text: Meet uv, a super-fast potion tool. It brews a cauldron called .venv right inside your project folder.

ee849083.text: Read the real recipe and answer my questions. Then one spell brews it all!

d5809e2e.text: Planting seeds is only the start. A forest also needs its animals back!

8d4dfba4.text: New trick: the crates float down. Type the word before a crate lands!

73915c9e.text: Four animals need different things. Read carefully!

8f703e7e.text: Our Ozarks forest was only bare for winter. But here a storm knocked trees down, so we help the gap.

d3ade246.text: Last stop: Borneo! Orangutans, hornbills and gibbons are waiting for their forest.

35b8764c.text: Some seeds can't ride a drone. Think before you load!

9122b5da.text: Read what each animal needs, then load the right habitat helpers on my drone.

c8682c97.text: Now type the growing word to jump 3 years ahead. Watch the NDVI chart climb!

f4182443.text: An animal came home! Type its name to say welcome.

aaff9170.text: My drones are ready. Next stop: the Fly island!

de37c1a2.text: Welcome to the Roll Factory, I'm Mo! We turn old toilet-paper rolls into seed pods for the drones.

167fc8a0.text: First we fill rolls with our own hands. Then we crack the factory's secret formulas!

82ca9a1d.text: The factory is humming! Seeds, rolls, trips and batteries: all planned.

51061761.text: This empty roll is a seed pod. Tap the dashed slots, or hold Space, to fill it with acorns.

3243b54e.text: My field drone carries 4 rolls per trip. Load the rolls and launch!

6be53258.text: Different seeds, different sizes! A tiny pine seed is nothing like a big acorn.

cefea148.text: Press Space to load a roll and Enter to launch. Don't leave any rolls behind!

36d41387.text: Time for the real thing: your site's mission, with ReSeed's real numbers!

d47244ba.text: Guess first, then stuff each seed into a roll and count what comes out.

a7932dec.text: Each machine needs one answer. Remember: rolls, batteries and days always round up.

4fd9214d.text: Full to the brim, but is it really full? Let's pour in some water and see!

bc69a847.text: All delivered, but we used some extra trips! Taking full loads would need fewer.

f53c1f78.text: All delivered! Two full trips, and one trip with just two rolls.

8e85d021.text: Smaller seeds, more per roll! The factory uses one tiny formula for all of them, ready to crack it?

22d0cdfc.text: Mission planned! Rolls stuffed, batteries counted, and way cheaper than planting by hand.

bac10ff8.text: No wind today. Press DROP and watch where the acorns land.

18796379.text: The acorns kept flying forward with the drone! That is inertia.

5635fe1d.text: This patch is close to the flag. Change the speed or height, then drop.

9739ee16.text: Now a far patch. Fast seeds fly farther, and high seeds fall for longer.

d22aa19f.text: These Paricá seeds from the Amazon fall slower than acorns. The drone just hovers.

48fb98fe.text: 💡 Slow down! At 1 m/s the acorns barely move forward.

c8cf1714.text: 💡 Fly lower and slower. Low seeds spend less time in the wind.

f930a8ac.text: Now real wind, 4 m/s from behind. It blows harder high up: look at the arrows.

dc18d12f.text: Which seed fits the MOST times into one roll?

eedfcb02.text: 💡 Try 7 m/s and fly high, like 20 m or more.

9fff9a5d.text: Uh oh, a headwind blows towards us. It pushes seeds backwards!

9984f10b.text: 💡 Fly low (about 5 m) and fast (about 5 m/s).

14174029.text: Windy day: 5 m/s! Every seed has its own terminal velocity, its top falling speed.

784f04fa.text: 💡 The patch is close. Pick the seed that falls fastest.

6a8e7923.text: Fast-falling seeds land near and slow ones drift far. Pick the seed for this patch.

b9924082.text: The Sierra needs pine seeds right here, close by. Same wind.

63980934.text: Turn up my wind machine so the wind carries the seeds onto the patch.

103c3766.text: 💡 Fly lower, about 8 to 9 m. Less time falling means less drift.

aa71b182.text: 💡 Backward flick throws the seeds back at about 3 m/s.

7eef521f.text: This patch is far downwind. Which seed will the wind carry that far?

fc384ac8.text: This big meadow needs acorns spread out, not in one heap.

d34fb4fa.text: You can't change the seed now. What else can you change?

09dce174.text: 💡 Spin spread: the drone spins and seeds fly out in a ring.

3a75bb6b.text: A tall tree stands past the patch. The drone must brake, but the seeds must fly on.

0925e9a3.text: 💡 Pick the slowest-falling seed: the pine seed with its papery wing removed.

f147e05c.text: 💡 Jerk back: the drone brakes hard and the seeds keep going. That's our demo-day move!

2a799583.text: My drone has four ways to let seeds go: the release modes.

a659fd96.text: This is your forest! ReSeed's physics model estimated a seed drop for it, with the same math as this game.

c07298af.text: G'day, I'm Koa from Kangaroo Island! Welcome to my seed drop range.

9bfb9820.text: In this game, let go before each patch, a little upwind. My computer marks where the seeds should land.

85067d38.text: Press DROP when the red target sits on a patch. You have 4 rolls for 3 patches.

a82a77c3.text: We fly at 3 m/s, but the patch is right under the flag. Which mode cancels our speed?

0b9bd8a4.text: Seeds can drift as they fall. Their starting speed, gravity and moving air all shape their path.

912ee5af.text: Next stop: Drone Academy. Let's earn your pilot wings!

8bba3d78.text: Wind pushes falling seeds sideways. Slow-falling seeds spend longer drifting.

54ec5dd9.text: Acorns fall fast, but pine seeds with their wings removed float down slowly. Let's use that!

ac2c6bdb.text: Same seeds, four tricks: hatch drop, jerk back, backward flick and spin spread.

4b890dde.text: Welcome to the Seed Library! Every native seed ReSeed can drop has a record here.

64897b40.text: A drone can only plant what we load. Let's find the right seeds for every forest!

2750224d.text: Tables, queries, keys and JSON: you did real database work today!

53177a9b.text: The crates are packed with native seeds. Meet me on Fly island, mate!

822853e6.text: Read each library request at the top. Then click the right row, column or cell.

cb403dec.text: Hatch drop from 20 m at 4 m/s, with a 3 m/s wind from the side.

2c00dc31.text: Help letters are pouring in! Every forest needs its own native seeds.

a6ef7aa3.text: Bonza! You can predict where a seed cloud lands, just like ReSeed's physics model.

4438d433.text: Wonderful! Next level, a query finds rows for you in a blink.

3842465a.text: Whoa, every seed in the library came out! A WHERE block keeps only the rows you want.

3fc1256f.text: Queries are like magic spells for data. You just wrote five of them!

2ed346f1.text: Guess first! How far from the drop point will the seeds land?

662a53a7.text: Connect the keys first. Then see the same seed facts in three outfits: a table row, JSON and a Python dictionary.

26e64f6a.text: All keys linked! A JOIN follows a key from one table into the other.

7f1016a4.text: Same seed, three outfits: a table row, JSON and a Python dict. Find each field in all three!

566e0e49.text: Hoo hoo, same plus sign but two different spells! Numbers add up, but strings just stick together.

09feeb9a.text: Wait, zero comes first? Computers are funny, so my rotor number zero is my first rotor!

8b3987c7.text: That's a real trap! ReSeed's own NDVI spell takes red first, so its code always passes red, then NIR.

46cb278b.text: Crikey, minus ten percent? Our game let that drone use more charge than it had!

7afb99cf.text: Let's add a game safety check: if the trip is too long, skip that flight.

4190bc73.text: Welcome to my Spell Academy! Python spells tell a computer exactly what to do.

ec6d89b0.text: Beauty, Tuki skips that flight! Real pilots also plan the way home and keep spare power.

6b6b810f.text: Every spell has a crystal ball. Guess what it will show, then cast it and see!

3015ee89.text: You read, fixed and wrote real Python spells. ReSeed is built from spells just like these!

90d0f30f.text: A variable is a name for a value, like a label on a jar. print shows it in the crystal ball.

0824dc94.text: Let's build the NDVI spell from Goggles island!

babe43ed.text: A function is a spell you can use again and again. def makes it, and return sends back the answer.

d6973fe2.text: if, elif and else let a spell choose. Python checks from the top and stops at the first True.

923a5776.text: A for loop repeats a spell for every item in a list. Perfect for twelve months of NDVI!

9d4985dc.text: This is a challenge spell. Take your time, and the hints will help you.

4431ed1e.text: Hoo, welcome to Check island, detective! Before we save a forest, we must be sure it really is a forest.

e8e68d1e.text: Splendid detective work! You sorted tiles, raced ForestNet and used the 1-in-4 rule.

c2040d80.text: Next stop: Brain Builder. Let's find out how ForestNet's brain works inside!

f6c8719a.text: And the drone class? I'm putting that one on my fridge!

5939cc47.text: Press F for forest and N for not forest, or tap the big buttons. Quick, detective!

69689155.text: Some pictures are tricky: lawns, farm fields, winter forests. Race ForestNet and see who is right!

23654b75.text: We know the true answer for every picture. One step forward for each right answer!

d5701fd9.text: ReSeed only helps places that were forest. If at least 1 tile in 4 is forest, it is forest land.

43051e98.text: If not, ReSeed says STOP and looks somewhere else. Guess first, then scan!

d7ac122a.text: A tricky case! This rainforest in Rondônia was cut down, and today much of it looks like cow pasture.

35ea6a1c.text: Which picture should ForestNet judge: the old one or the new one? You decide.

09b62488.text: Now the real ForestNet sorts the same tiles. It runs right here, inside your web browser!

c2d1c44f.text: Perfect match! You and ForestNet think alike, detective.

8875633f.text: Look at the tiles with a ⚡. Tap them: was ForestNet sure, or was it a coin flip?

f3401512.text: Oh dear, today's picture hides the lost forest! Try the old picture.

6993ddd5.text: See? The new picture could make ReSeed say STOP, so it judges the old one.

54e0ca5c.text: Yes! The old picture still shows the forest, so ReSeed can plan to plant it back.

060a6195.text: G'day! Every drone in my fleet has a name and a battery, so let's make a class: a blueprint for drones.

2dee213c.text: Brilliant! The old picture shows forest land, so the rescue goes on, but peek at the new one.

865f4be6.text: Exactly! Burned forest still counts as forest land, so ReSeed can plan to replant it.

702eee90.text: Careful! After the fire ForestNet might say not forest, so ReSeed judges the picture from before the fire.

1da5366b.text: 💡 Think: what did this place look like before it was cut down?

06e02e66.text: The Dixie Fire burned in 2021. Which picture should ReSeed's forest check use?

2744d4e4.text: These code screens, called terminals, show Python-style code. Change it, and the room changes!

b8cffab6.text: Whoo-hoo! Thank you, Sprout. A GPU can make training much faster!

ab05cd67.text: Whoo! I'm stuck on a high ledge. That door opens when NDVI, our plant-green score, is 0.6 or more.

8d764ddd.text: Squawk! Koa is locked in the database room. Find Koa's forest type, called a biome, to open the cage!

4c428c89.text: Be careful what you bring to land burned by fire!

cabcbc79.text: In our game, the seeds are planted in Rondônia. Now the animals need help to come home!

80ae42b8.text: ReSeed keeps checking the NDVI from space every year. Greener leaves are a good clue, but not proof the forest is back!

7b0868e2.text: A satellite checks the NDVI again every year. In our game version, look how it climbed!

adb226f2.text: G'day! This is my home, Kangaroo Island. Most trees grew back after the fire, and in our game we help one small patch that didn't.

a8d034f6.text: Next stop: Cloud Sweeper. Let's clean up those cloudy pictures!

1775c8e1.text: Hi, I'm Tuki! I carry messages between the forest and the satellites.

c49a45af.text: Use the arrow keys, the buttons, or drag the globe. Fly the crosshair to each target!

035723f5.text: ReSeed needs fresh pictures from space. Let's learn to aim, time and snap!

23936791.text: Every place on Earth has two numbers. Latitude goes north and south, longitude goes east and west.

e1391207.text: Wow! You can find any spot, time a pass, dodge clouds and read pixels.

f5fe320e.text: Meet Sentinel-2: twin satellites with cameras that see 10 m pixels.

4f1ca251.text: When the camera frame turns green over the target, press SPACE or tap SNAP!

35e41680.text: Snap only the clear passes. If it's too cloudy, wait 5 days for the next pass!

9b559d69.text: Ketapang in Borneo is very cloudy. ReSeed uses a 30% cloud limit for this site.

8d33be00.text: My favourite tree is in this forest! Let's see what a drone and two satellites can see.

f40a8e28.text: Each pixel is one colour for one square of ground. Bigger squares show fewer details.

c5687d7a.text: G'day! Not every satellite takes pictures: GPS satellites help my drone know where it is.

092c3023.text: First, sort the satellites. Then use three GPS distances to find my lost drone!

5300c3e8.text: Minus means south for latitude and west for longitude. Now find My Site!

d82d7c1b.text: Not quite! Minus means west for longitude and south for latitude.

3eec5917.text: Yes! A minus longitude means west, and a minus latitude means south.

80abbf81.text: ReSeed's Rondônia site is at -9.35, -64.35. What does the minus in -64.35 mean?

7ff6be63.text: Now look through Sentinel-2. Can you still see my tree?

5a389135.text: Same spot, two dates! The old Landsat photo shows the forest before it was lost.

4473631b.text: Now fly Landsat! Its pixels are 30 m, but its photo album goes back to 1984.

8bd3cfcf.text: Real Ketapang is just as cloudy! Here is the log of pictures ReSeed really kept.

8a3f3827.text: Right! One pixel is 10 m wide, about one tree crown, so Sentinel-2 sees forest patches, not single trees.

14e10363.text: Look again: it melted into the green. One pixel is as wide as a whole tree crown!

e7cd013c.text: Here is Landsat at 30 m. Which pictures still show the small clearing by the river?

6ae66eb7.text: Yes! Landsat's big 30 m pixels blur small things away, but big patches still show up.

e2934b77.text: So why does ReSeed still use blurry Landsat?

3f8cd7ad.text: Look at the circles: in Landsat the small clearing blurs away. Its 30 m pixels are too big.

34295b0d.text: Yes! Old Landsat pictures show what a forest looked like long ago.

8600dd5c.text: Each 10 m pixel is a small square of land, and 100 of them make one hectare. ReSeed skips patches smaller than 50 pixels (0.5 ha).

d1847901.text: Two circles cross at two spots. Which one is it?

45aa79c7.text: The drone is somewhere on this circle. One distance is not enough!

b31793f0.text: Not quite. Landsat's album goes back to 1984, so we can see the old forest.

4afc9938.text: Only one spot sits on all three circles. Tap it!

a3c608a9.text: Great sorting! Now my drone is lost over the forest, so let's listen to the GPS satellites.

b19aa721.text: Under thick trees, GPS has a harder time. The bigger circle shows all the places the drone might be.

02183a07.text: 💡 Watch the gold frame. Press when it turns green and says NOW!

6353f8e6.text: Real receivers use 4 or more satellites. A phone is good to about 5 m under open sky!

b9ebdaf1.text: 💡 Read the cloud number first: over 30% means let that pass go by!
